scenario.name: Microsoft MSTIC, Volexity & CISA ED 21-02 DFIR — Exchange HttpProxy, MSExchange Management & OAB Webshell Forensics
scenario.overview: Forensic auditors reconstruct a break-in at a corporate mail building by tracing three linked clues: first the front-desk forwarding slips that misrouted a stranger into the rear office, next the management ledger recording a tampered address-book path, and finally the fresh workshop printouts proving a hidden control page ran commands. In this scenario (T1190, Microsoft MSTIC, Volexity & CISA ED 21-02 DFIR, Exchange HttpProxy, MSExchange Management & OAB Webshell Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: exchange Frontend HttpProxy Log Analysis, then exchange Management Log, then aSP.NET Dynamic Compilation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Exchange Frontend HttpProxy Log Analysis, then Exchange Management Log, then ASP.NET Dynamic Compilation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application: Exchange HttpProxy SSRF)

stages.title: Stage 2: Exchange Management Log (MSExchange Management EventID 1) Set-OabVirtualDirectory & New-MailboxExportRequest
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1505.003 - Server Software Component: Web Shell via Exchange Cmdlet)
stages.description: Following the timestamp into the supervisor office ledger, investigators catch an administrative order rewriting an offline address-book web link so its description field hides an executable page script. Using the proxied backend session, the actor invokes the Exchange Management cmdlet Set-OabVirtualDirectory (injecting JScript webshell code into the ExternalUrl property) followed by ResetOABVirtualDirectory (or New-MailboxExportRequest -FilePath "\\127.0.0.1\C$\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\supp.aspx") to write the configuration to disk. stages.subtitle: Execution (T1505.003 - Temporary ASP.NET Files Artifact & w3wp.exe Child Shell)
stages.description: Even if the intruder tears down the wall flyer afterward, the building print shop retains freshly compiled proof plates in its temporary drawer and security cameras catch the mailroom clerk carrying heavy workshop tools. When the external actor requests POST /aspnet_client/supp.aspx, IIS w3wp.exe compiles the page via csc.exe into C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\Temporary ASP.NET Files\root\*\App_Web_*.dll (persisting even if supp.aspx is later deleted from inetpub) and spawns cmd.exe under w3wp.exe (-ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool") as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with EventID=1 , Sysmon ProcessCreate + 11 , Temporary ASP.NET DLL, ParentAppPool=w3wp.exe -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" , SYSTEM, CompiledAssemblyArtifact=Temporary ASP.NET Files\...\App_Web_supp.aspx.cdcab7d2.dll so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Sysmon EventID 11: C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\Temporary ASP.NET Files\root\...\App_Web_supp.aspx.cdcab7d2.dll (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 11: C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\Temporary ASP.NET Files\r so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1505.003 during "ASP.NET Dynamic Compilation , Temporary ASP.NET Files & w3wp.exe Child Shell , Sysmon EventID 1 & 11" , When the external actor requests POST /aspnet_client/supp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe (-ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool") -> Image=C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , Sysmon EventID 1: ParentImage=C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\w3wp.exe , -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" -> Ima so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1505.003 during "ASP.NET Dynamic Compilation , Temporary ASP.NET Files & w3wp.exe Child Shell , Sysmon EventID 1 & 11" , When the external actor requests POST /aspnet_client/supp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ w3wp.exe -ap "MSExchangeOWAAppPool" spawning cmd.exe /c whoami / ⇠#3 ACK 1) from Node ③ (#3 Exchange Frontend HttpProxy) to Node ④ (#4 Exchange Backend EWS / ECP), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 OAB ExternalUrl & w3wp.exe).
